title: SEBI's New Study on Retail Derivatives Losses in July
description: SEBI is preparing to release a fresh study in July on the profit and loss outcomes of individual traders in equity derivatives. This new review builds upon ea.

faq.a: Equity derivatives are financial contracts whose value is derived from an underlying equity asset, such as a stock or a stock index. Common types include futures and options, allowing investors to speculate on price movements or hedge existing positions.

faq.q: Why is SEBI releasing a new study on derivatives losses?
faq.a: SEBI is releasing a new study to update its previous findings on retail investors' profit and loss outcomes in the equity derivatives segment. This ongoing monitoring helps the regulator assess market health, identify potential risks to investors, and inform future policy decisions.

Generally, derivatives are considered high-risk instruments, especially for retail investors due to the inherent leverage, complexity, and time-bound nature of many contracts. While they can be used for hedging, speculative trading carries significant potential for capital loss.

faq.q: How are profits from derivatives trading taxed in India?
faq.a: Profits from derivatives trading (futures and options) are typically treated as business income for tax purposes in India, not as capital gains. This means they are added to your total income and taxed at your applicable slab rate. Losses can generally be set off against other business income.

faq.q: What is the difference between futures and options?
faq.a: A futures contract obligates the buyer to purchase, or the seller to sell, an asset at a predetermined price on a specified future date. An options contract, however, gives the buyer the *right*, but not the obligation, to buy or sell an asset at a specific price before a certain date, while the seller has the obligation.

faq.q: Where can I find SEBI's official reports on derivatives?
faq.a: SEBI publishes its reports and research papers on its official website under the 'Reports' or 'Research' sections. You can typically find studies related to market analysis and investor behaviour there.
